newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian rubber closes down on adjustments.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian rubber closes down on adjustments.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower on technical adjustment, with traders reporting weak consumer demand apart from some light interest for the SMR 20.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted April RSS1 buyer at 298.50 cents ($1.20) a kg, down one cent from Monday. April SMR20 buyer ended half cent lower at 285.
"We had an inquiry from Korea for a couple of containers of SMR 20 at between 283-285 (Malaysian cents)," said a trader. "Otherwise, the market was pretty quiet, with U.S. and Europe extremely down."
Traders offered the SMR20 at 286 cents a kg, SMR CV at 352, SMR L at 332, SMR 5 at 295, SMR 10 at 287 and drum latex FOB at 236.
A further retreat in prices was expected this week as Malaysian producers competed with their Indonesian counterparts who were quoting lower, said local traders.
The INRO five-day average was at 229.50 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 24 from 229.91 on March 21. The daily indicator was at 229.73 from 229.12.
